Dominus, Dominī m.

noun, second declension

Classically a master or owner; in the Vulgate and the Church God (Greek Κύριος) and Christ (Lewis & Short). The vocative is Domine; Dominus noster, Our Lord.

Examples

  • Dominus regit mē, et nihil mihi deerit

    The Lord is my shepherd; I shall want nothingVulg. Ps. 22 (23), 1

  • Vōs vocātis mē Magister et Domine, et bene dīcitis: sum etenim.

    You call me Teacher and Lord, and you are right, for so I am.Vulg. Jo. 13.13

See also God, Lord, have mercy, the Lord’s Prayer.
